[LGRA.10.1.3] **Nothing in a rule's RHS refers to a binding after it is
withdrawn.** A rule's actions run in source order, and `withdraw b` removes the
fact bound to `b` when it runs ([LSCO.4.5.9]). No action after it in the same
RHS may refer to `b`: not by reading a slot of `b`, anywhere in the action or in
a body nested in it, and not by withdrawing `b` again. The compiler **must**
refuse such a reference with `DS_VALIDATE_WITHDRAWN_BINDING_USED`, at the
action that contains it, naming the binding and the `withdraw` before it. A body
nested in a later action — a call continuation, an `after` body — counts,
although it runs later: the values it reads are captured from the fact when the
action containing it runs ([LCCO.5.2]), and that is after the `withdraw`. An
action before the `withdraw` may refer to `b` freely. A `logical` emit after the
`withdraw` in the same RHS is refused whether or not it refers to `b`
([LLOG.11.9]).

The same rule holds inside a nested body that itself withdraws `b`
([LGRA.10.1.4]): nothing after that `withdraw` in the body may refer to `b`. An
action of the outer RHS after the one containing that body may still refer to
`b`, because the body runs later.
